summary.pack_description:
Get in on the playoff excitement with 'Playoff Bound' – a collection that includes one key highlight per playoff-bound team from the final month of the regular season. 'Playoff Bound' offers a glimpse into the plays that contributed to their ascension into playoff contention. 

Featuring jaw-dropping apples and late-game heroics from Aleksander Barkov, Evgeny Kuznetsov, Ryan Nugent-Hopkins, Vincent Trocheck, Sean Walker, Matt Duchene, and more!

Each pack contains 2 Playoff Bound highlights, 1 mystery Core highlight that could be from Base (25%), Base 2023-24 (25%), Stadiums & Skylines (25%), or Playoff Bound (25%), and 1 mystery highlight that could be from Light the Lamp (29%), Guardians of the Net (29%), Next-Gen Class (20%), Opening Ice: Elites (10%), Opening Ice (10%), Cause for a Celly: ‘90s (1.9%), or The Greatest Achievements (<1%).

release.name: Playoff Bound Encore Pack
release.description:
Sale Starts: Thursday May 23, 2024 at 1PM ET / 10AM PT

 

Price: $9 USD

# Packs Available: 2,000. Edition numbers are distributed randomly.

 

Purchase Limit: Five (5) pack limit per person for the first 24 hours; limit increased to ten (10) pack limit per person afterwards. Once the “Buy Now” process has started, users will have 10 minutes to complete checkout before the pack(s) is released for another collector to purchase.

 

Highlights Per Pack: 4

Pack Contents (Highlight Rarity, Edition Size):

  • Two (2) highlights from Playoff Bound (Core #/1500)
  • One (1) highlight with the following probabilities:
    • 25% Base (Core #/1500)
    • 25% Base 2023-24 (Core #/1500)
    • 25% Stadiums & Skylines (Core #/1500)
    • 25% Playoff Bound (Core #/1500)
  • One (1) highlight with the following probabilities:
    • 29% Light the Lamp (Limited #/500)
    • 29% Guardians of the Net (Limited #/500)
    • 20% Next-Gen Class (Limited #/500)
    • 10% Opening Ice: Elites (Rare #/250)
    • 10% Opening Ice (Rare #/250)
    • 1.9% Cause for a Celly: ‘90s (Epic #/100)
    • 0.1% The Greatest Achievements (Legendary #10)

 

Payment Methods Accepted: Most major credit and debit cards. Payments will be made via registered payment processor MoonPay where available; where not available, payments will be processed via Stripe.

 

Fan Marketplace: Packs and highlights are eligible to be sold to other collectors in the NHL Breakaway fan marketplace. See FAQ.

 

Transferability: Packs and highlights can be exchanged in the Trade Lounge™ with other NHL Breakaway users.

 

Blockchain: Polygon

 

Sets Included:

  • Full Highlights List
  • Playoff Bound, Series 1 - Preview
  • Base 2023-24, Series 1 - Preview
  • Stadiums & Skylines, Series 1 - Preview
  • Base, Series 1 - Preview
  • Light the Lamp, Series 1 - Preview
  • Guardians of the Net, Series 1 - Preview
  • Next-Gen Class, Series 1 - Preview
  • Opening Ice: Elites, Series 1 - Preview
  • Opening Ice, Series 1 - Preview
  • Cause for a Celly: ‘90s, Series 1 - Preview
  • The Greatest Achievements, Series 1 - Preview

 

Collection Guarantee: Series 1 highlights will only be distributed during Series 1, which ends ~September 2024. We will not issue more than the edition limit we have set. Any editions not distributed in packs will not be distributed after the series end date (See FAQ for “Uncirculated Editions”)

 

All sales subject to Terms

summary.name: Aleksander Barkov
summary.description:
During a powerplay midway through the second period against conference opponent New York Rangers, Aleksander Barkov makes an incredible play to earn the assist and get the Panthers on the board.  Leading the rush up the ice, Barkov dishes the puck over to Carter Verhaeghe who quickly returns it back.  Barkov then juggles the puck to elude a defender before diving to send the puck over to Sam Reinhart who slams it in the net.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Evgeny Kuznetsov
summary.description:
Facing a conference opponent in the Florida Panthers, Evgeny Kuznetsov nets his first goal as a member of the Carolina Hurricanes. Defenseman Jalen Chatfield finds Kuznetsov who is positioned on the far side. Receiving the pass, Kuznetsov maneuvers toward the goal and fires a wrist shot that hits the mark. His celebration, characterized by his signature "bird celly," ignites cheers from the Hurricanes' faithful crowd.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Tommy Novak
summary.description:
Beginning with a stretch pass from goaltender Juuse Saros, Tommy Novak receives the puck just before the offensive blueline and immediately heads toward the net. With a slick backhand-to-forehand move, he jukes the defender and then sends a wrister that finds the back of the net against the division-rival Colorado Avalanche.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Kyle Palmieri
summary.description:
Having already scored the first two goals of the game, Kyle Palmieri nets his third in the first period for the natural hat trick. As the puck gets bounced around near the front of the net, Jean-Gabriel Pageau eventually emerges with it and spots Palmieri up near the point. Palmieri moves it over to Ryan Pulock who makes a pass of the goalie pad getting kicked out right to Palmieri who buries it into the net.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Sean Walker
summary.description:
Acquired in a trade ahead of the 2023-24 deadline and playing in his fourth game as a member of the Colorado Avalanche, defenseman Sean Walker came up big in a game versus the rival Edmonton Oilers. After notching his first goal with the new team earlier in the game, Walker leveled the score with just over five minutes remaining in the third period with his second tally. As Casey Mittelstadt skates behind the net with the puck, Walker jumps into the slot from the point where he receives the pass and blasts a one-timer past the netminder.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: John Carlson
summary.description:
At 34 years old and playing in his 15th NHL season, all with the Washington Capitals, defenseman John Carlson continues to make an impact on the ice. Facing a divisional opponent, the Philadelphia Flyers, Carlson netted a goal late in the second period which proved to be the game winner. Positioned down low near the net, Carlson capitalized on a rebound generated by a Rasmus Sandin point shot, executing a wraparound maneuver to beat the opposing goaltender.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Cam Talbot
summary.description:
After an errant turnover by the LA Kings, Cam Talbot comes up with a remarkable diving stop on Tim Stützle.  Despite Claude Giroux's cross-ice pass seemingly leaving Stützle with a wide-open net, Talbot manages to get across and snatch the puck with his glove just in time. This impressive display comes in Talbot's inaugural season with the LA Kings, where he made a total of 28 saves against his former team from the previous season.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Ryan Nugent-Hopkins
summary.description:
In the final two minutes of regulation, as the Oilers found themselves trailing 1-0, Ryan Nugent-Hopkins makes a tremendous defensive effort getting a stick on Danton Heinen’s shot attempt at the empty net just in time.  This game saving play allowed Leon Draisaitl to even up the score on the very next shift with only 80 seconds remaining in the third period.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Matt Duchene
summary.description:
Speeding through the neutral zone, Matt Duchene collects the puck near center ice to head down for a 2-on-1 with Tyler Seguin. Gaining steam, Duchene looks as if he is going to shoot the puck – fooling both the defenseman and the goalie before he makes a beautiful behind-the-back feed to Seguin who finishes the play.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Bobby McMann
summary.description:
Bobby McMann nets his first of two goals in the game off of an impressive shift by the Toronto Maple Leafs. As the puck is dumped softly into the offensive zone, Timothy Liljegren chases it down to advance the puck further to John Tavares. Prior to receiving the puck, Tavares takes a look to see McMann open in the slot. Tavares spins with the puck on his backhand to send the puck out to McMann who buries it. McMann finished the night with 2 goals and 1 assist.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Nils Hoglander
summary.description:
Beginning with a strip of the puck by Connor Garland in the defensive zone, he advances it up the ice to Elias Pettersson who moves it over to the streaking Nils Hoglander. With a clear path to the net, Hoglander freezes the goalie with a fake shot before shifting it to the backhand and roofing it upstairs for his second goal of the game.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Keegan Kolesar
summary.description:
In the final two minutes of the third period of a tied game, Keegan Kolesar scores the game winner with 80 seconds remaining on the clock. As the puck gets moved over to Brett Howden on the left side, Kolesar positioned on the other side heads directly to the net where he stops. Howden makes a power move to the net where the puck squirts loose directly to Kolesar who buries it past the netminder for the decisive tally.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Danton Heinen
summary.description:
Holding a one-goal lead in the final five minutes of the third period, Danton Heinen snipes one past the netminder to create a two-goal cushion for the Boston Bruins. The play unfolds from a blocked shot in the defensive zone, initiating an offensive opportunity for Heinen. Charging down the left side, Heinen snaps one tops shelf from near the face-off circle. With Philadelphia scoring moments later, Heinen’s tally proved to be the game winner.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Anthony Cirelli
summary.description:
As the puck gets moved around the boards, Anthony Cirelli gives chase and beats Jack Eichel to it to spring ahead on a 2-on-0 break with Brandon Hagel. Heading toward the net, Cirelli moves the puck over to Hagel who gives it right back for Cirelli to fire it past the netminder for the shorty.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Neal Pionk
summary.description:
Originating from a battle for the puck along the boards, the puck squirts loose to Mason Appleton who quickly locates Neal Pionk on the far side. Pionk breaks for the net using his body to shield the puck from the defender and rips it home past the goalie. The first-period goal proved to be the game winner in a 3-0 Jets victory.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Vincent Trocheck
summary.description:
Centerman, Vincent Trocheck, who set a new career high this year for assists in a single season showcases a beauty here. Carrying the puck on a two-on-one, he opens up on the forehand, seemingly prepared to shoot. As the defenseman slides on the ice trying to take away the passing option, Trocheck sauces it perfectly over to Panarin for the sweet apple.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Base
summary.description: The Series 1 Base set is a collection of meaningful highlights from each team in the League that occurred during the 2022-23 season.

summary.name: Base 2023-24
summary.description: Get ready to relive the adrenaline-packed start of the 2023-24 NHL season – everything from game-breaking clappers to hat tricks to how-did-he-get-there saves! Featuring rising stars, savvy veterans, and comeback kings like Alex DeBrincat, Mika Zibanejad, Sean Couturier, William Nylander, Corey Perry, Mark Sheifele and more!

summary.name: Stadiums & Skylines
summary.description: Introducing "Stadiums & Skylines," a set that celebrates the thrilling past and present moments from a diverse array of NHL outdoor games. This unique collection showcases iconic stadiums and breathtaking skylines as the backdrop to unforgettable hockey events. Immerse yourself in the excitement of these outdoor spectacles with "Stadiums & Skylines," where the magic of hockey meets the awe-inspiring settings that make these games truly extraordinary.

summary.name: Ray Bourque
summary.description:
After an illustrious career spanning 22 seasons, Ray Bourque finally achieved the ultimate triumph of hoisting the Stanley Cup. At the age of 40, in what would be his final year in professional hockey, Bourque fulfilled his long-standing dream of winning this highly coveted trophy. This remarkable achievement added to the numerous accolades he had already earned, including holding the record for the most goals, assists and points in NHL history by a defenseman, along with five Norris Trophy awards. Leading up to this historic victory, Bourque showcased his invaluable contributions by scoring the game-winning goal during Game 3 of the Stanley Cup Final. With the game tied and a power play in progress, a crucial faceoff ensued in the early moments of the third period. Bourque skillfully seized control of the puck after it was won back to him, swiftly gliding towards the center of the ice before unleashing a powerful slapshot that flew past the formidable Martin Brodeur. Then, on June 9, 2001, following a resounding 3-1 victory by the Colorado Avalanche in Game 7, team captain Joe Sakic received the coveted Stanley Cup from Commissioner Gary Bettman. In a deeply significant gesture, Sakic promptly skated over to Bourque, personally handing off the cherished trophy to the deserving veteran. This poignant moment served as the culmination of Bourque's extraordinary career, marking the pinnacle of his accomplishments and forever etching his name into hockey lore.

summary.name: Mario Lemieux
summary.description:
In a defining moment of the 1991 Stanley Cup Final against the Minnesota North Stars, Mario Lemieux delivered a goal that would become iconic. This extraordinary play paved the way for the Pittsburgh Penguins to secure their first-ever Stanley Cup victory. With the Penguins holding a 2-1 lead late in the second period, Lemieux takes control of the puck deep in his own zone and swiftly sets off, building momentum as he moves up the ice. Crossing the blueline, Lemieux showcases his unmatched skill by gracefully maneuvering past two Minnesota defenders. With a quick shift of the puck onto his backhand, he expertly places it beyond the reach of goaltender Jon Casey. The goal not only showcased Lemieux's brilliance but also propelled the Penguins closer to their championship triumph. Throughout the playoffs, Lemieux displayed incredible prowess, leading to him being awarded the prestigious Conn Smythe Trophy. His exceptional performance included registering an impressive 44 points in just 23 games, ranking as the second-highest number of playoff points ever recorded in a single season in NHL history.
